Subject: Redwood MSA redline (output/training items)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the call this week. Attached is our redline of the MSA and the order form focusing on IP/usage language. Legal flagged three items we need explicit confirmation on before procurement can move to exec approval:

1) Output ownership: Acme requests assignment of rights for model outputs generated from our inputs (examples: patient-facing copy, clinical summaries). They want a clear assignment clause or an explicit carveout that gives them exclusive rights to outputs.
2) Training & feedback: They want confirmation that Redwood will not use Acme data / logs for model training without an affirmative opt-in, and any feedback or telemetry used for improvement must be aggregated and anonymized with evidence.
3) Telemetry & logs: Retention window and access controls — Acme needs audit logs and SOC2 evidence showing tenant isolation.

Can you confirm which of these we can accept as-is, which require a counter, and what evidence we can provide for procurement? We attached the redline as Acme_MSA_Redline_v2.docx.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — the procurement review board meets next Wednesday.

Best,
Sara

Sara — thanks for the redline and the clear list. Looping in Laura (legal), Ben (product/ops) and Neha (sales ops) so we can triage quickly.

Quick answers up front:
- Output ownership: we typically license outputs to customers for their use, with an option for assignment in narrow cases tied to procurement terms. We do not automatically assign IP for outputs in the standard MSA.
- Training & feedback: we support explicit opt-out for training; default is anonymized telemetry for platform improvements unless the customer chooses to opt out.
- Telemetry & logs: we can provide SOC2 documentation and tenant-scoped audit logs; retention windows are configurable by plan.

Laura/Ben — can you confirm specifics we can commit to and propose language or examples we can send back to Acme? Sara, we'll aim to get a redline back by EOD Monday so you have time for procurement review.

Thanks,

Subject: RE: Redwood MSA redline (output/training items) — legal points

Karthik / team — reviewing Acme's redline now. High-level legal positions and recommended language below (I tried to keep changes narrow to preserve our standard commercial terms):

1) Output ownership
- Risk: Full assignment of outputs in perpetuity could impact our ability to provide the same model service to other customers and may create downstream licensing obligations.
- Recommendation: Accept a broad, irrevocable, perpetual license to the customer to use outputs for their products and services instead of assignment. Add a carveout that permits us to use outputs for internal debugging and to provide the service to other customers in non-identifying ways. Proposed clause: "Customer is granted a perpetual, worldwide, exclusive license to reproduce, modify, and distribute Outputs generated by the Service in connection with Customer's products; Redwood retains the right to use aggregated and de-identified Outputs for service operation and improvement."

2) Training & feedback
- Risk: Using raw customer content to train base models without consent is a compliance and retention risk.
- Recommendation: Offer an explicit "training opt-in" checkbox in the order form. For customers who opt-out, add: "Redwood will not use Customer Content, Outputs, or telemetry for model training or improving model weights without Customer's prior written consent." For customers who opt-in, define anonymization/aggregation standards and provide evidence (audit report) on request.

3) Telemetry & logs
- Recommendation: Commit to SOC2 Type II attestation (we can provide the report under NDA) and provide tenant-scoped audit logs with a 90-day default retention and options to extend as a paid add-on. If Acme needs longer retention for audits, tie it to a procurement add-on.

Actionable next steps:
- I will produce a clean redline (commented) that swaps assignment for a perpetual license and adds an opt-in/opt-out training paragraph.
- Ben, please confirm implementation/ops feasibility for audit logs, 90-day default, and a paid retention extension.
- Karthik/Neha — once we have Ben's feasibility and my redline, send to Acme with a short note offering the order-form toggle for training opt-in and an example SOC2 access process.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Laura / team — quick ops notes: we can support the approach Laura proposed with the following constraints and options: 

- Output license vs assignment: purely legal; no infra change required.
- Training opt-out: we already support per-customer opt-out flags; opt-out prevents any customer content from entering training pipelines. Implementation: toggle at provisioning + record in config store. We will add an entry in the onboarding checklist and surface it in the Console.
- Telemetry: tenant-scoped audit logs are available; default retention 90 days is fine. If Acme wants 1+ year retention we need to provision additional storage and the procurement team should budget for the retention add-on (estimate: $2k/month per additional 6 months for their expected volume). We can provide periodic export (S3) or longer retention as an enterprise feature.

I'll prepare an ops note for procurement with: (a) how to opt in/out, (b) a short runbook for requesting SOC2 under NDA, (c) cost estimate for extended retention.

Ben Carter
Head of Product Operations | Redwood Inference

Sara — thanks for the patience and the rapid review. Summary and proposed path for your procurement board: 

1) Output ownership: Redwood proposes to amend the MSA to grant Acme a perpetual, worldwide, exclusive license to Outputs for use in Acme's products and services. We cannot accept unrestricted assignment; the license will include a narrow carveout allowing Redwood to use aggregated/de-identified Outputs for platform improvements and debugging. Laura's redline attached.

2) Training & feedback: We will include an order-form toggle: "Training Opt-in" (default: opt-in to anonymized improvements). If Acme selects "opt-out," Redwood will not use Customer Content, Outputs, or telemetry for model training without written consent.

3) Telemetry & logs: Redwood can provide SOC2 Type II report under NDA and tenant-scoped audit logs with 90-day default retention. Extended retention or export is available as a paid add-on; Ben will provide a cost estimate.

Next steps / timeline:
- Today (EOD): Laura will send the clean redline (attached).
- Monday 09/04: Ben will send the procurement ops note + cost estimate for retention extension.
- By Tuesday 09/05 EOD: Karthik/Neha will deliver the redline + short cover note to Acme legal for procurement board.

Please let me know if that timeline works for Acme's procurement board. If you need executive escalation or a short legal call to resolve the last assignment vs license nuance, we can set up a 30-min slot tomorrow.

Thanks again — look forward to closing this.

Karthik
